newsitem.title: UK: Zinc zooms to 10-month highs on LME, copper sours.
newsitem.headline: Zinc zooms to 10-month highs on LME, copper sours.

text.p: Zinc held centre stage on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday afternoon, roaring to 10-month highs after a sizable LME stocks drawdown.
But copper was left in the dust after a promising start. It stalled at resistance and a bout of long liquidation demolished its gains.
Zinc's dramatic surge took off when an LME stocks drawdown of 11,975 tonnes attracted funds and speculators, traders said.
Prices steadily ratcheted up throughout the day, leapfrogging the initial $1,100 resistance level to end the afternoon kerb $39 stronger at $1,109 per tonne.
"It's the funds. The drawdown was substantial and once zinc got up above $1,080 it started looking very good technically," a trader said.

By contrast, copper tumbled sharply towards the end of the kerb from its perch around the $2,280 resistance level. It ended at $2,261, down $2 against Monday's kerb close but off $27 from the day's high.
"The gains were wiped out by long liquidation. Everyone thought it was going to get above $2,300 and when it didn't they got out," a trader said.
A smaller than expected rise in LME stocks of 200 tonnes had initially given copper the chance to break higher, traders said.
"There are bigger fish to fry at the moment than copper and aluminium right now," said another, referring to zinc's strength. "Those two may have done enough for now."
The premium of cash to three months copper narrowed by about $20 over the day, ending at around $165/$170, while the cash to February backwardation came in a similar amount to $110/$115.

Aluminium steadily notched lower after inventories rose by a modest 1,750 tonnes, and ended $16 down at $1,608. Dealers said sentiment was still bullish overall but prices needed to consolidate considering aluminium's overbought status.
Lead put in a solid performance, breaking back above the $700 level and touching $715, the highest since December 27. It was last $16 higher at $708.
It needed to get above the late December high of $723 to confirm that it was trending higher, analysts said.
Tin added to recent gains and ended the kerb $75 stronger at $6,035 after a decline in stocks. Its next target was the November high of $6,175.
Nickel came off highs after failing to advance above $7,300, but still ended $20 higher at $7,220.
